newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rally to record on rates, GDP.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rally to record on rates, GDP.

text.p: Mexican stocks extended earlier gains on Monday to post their fourth record close in five sessions on expectations of additional cuts in interest rates at the forthcoming primary auction.
"The market was very quiet as Wall Street was closed, but in good spirits due to expected rates cuts," said Carlos Ponce, research chief at Santander Investment in Mexico City.
"Also, indicators released last week bode well for this week's GDP figures," he added.
The leading IPC share index ended up 23.67 points, or 0.62 percent, at 3,850.44.
Mexico's Finance Ministry is due to release 1996 GDP figures on Wednesday.
Trading volume was lackluster at 50.6 million shares traded, due to the absence of U.S. investors and the fact that open outcry was suspended. A screen trading system called SENTRA was used instead.
U.S. financial markets were closed on Monday for Presidents Day.
"SENTRA worked very well, but the session lacked its usual atmosphere," a trader from the Abaco brokerage said.
On the broad market, a total of 109 stocks were traded, of which 53 ended up while 23 declined.
Traders said that speculative buying in the absence of U.S. investors pushed up prices for second-tier stocks like chemical company Penwalt and Maizoro, which headed the gainers' list.
"These stocks are easy to manipulate, so dealers took advantage of the lack of foreign investors in order to raise prices," one trader said.
Financial stocks headed the decliners' due to caution among investors, traders said, but after thin-volume deals, they said.
